# The PFTC model {.unnumbered}

This book is the teaching material for the Plant Functional Trait Courses (PFTC).
The courses is a hands-on end-to-end data life cylcle training in trait-based ecology.
More about the courses themselves is on the course [webpage](https://plantfunctionaltraitscourses.w.uib.no/).

Most ecology and field biology courses only cover part of the data life cycle (@data_lifecycle).

::: {.lifecycle}
```{=html}
{{< include images/data_lifecycle.svg >}}
```
:::

The PFTC model is teaches all parts of the data life cycle, from planning to data re-use (@pftc_model).
It adds three layers to the data life cycle: documentation, methods and technology, and community of practice.

::: {.lifecycle}
```{=html}
{{< include images/pftc_model.svg >}}
```
:::

### How to use the book

The chapters follow the course: [pre-course](plan_logistics.qmd), the [field course](first_days.qmd), and [post-course](course_evaluation.qmd).
Under each of those, the chapters are grouped by step: Plan, Design, Collect, and the steps that follow.
The four larger groups on the wheel — Create, Process, Share, and Re-use — overlap those times, so they are not the sidebar groups.
The PFTC model sits underneath that timeline.
The inner ring is the scientific process, in four parts: Create, Process, Share, and Re-use.
Around it, from the centre outward, are the documents, the methods, and the community.

A page that belongs to one of these carries a sign in the colour from the wheels.
Some pages are not part of a category, and those have no sign.

```{=html}
<div class="model-signs" aria-label="Colours used on the PFTC model">
<span class="sign sign-create">Create</span>
<span class="sign sign-process">Process</span>
<span class="sign sign-share">Share</span>
<span class="sign sign-reuse">Re-use</span>
<span class="sign sign-data">Data documentation</span>
<span class="sign sign-methods">Methods and technology</span>
<span class="sign sign-community">Community of practice</span>
</div>
```


### Funding

The Plant Functional Traits Courses acknowledge funding from the following sources:

**The Norwegian Research Council**
*ExperTS* - Experiments, Traits, Synthesis: Using knowledge from global ecological experiments to validate, assess, and improve trait-based theory. INTPART project 287784 2019 – 2023.
PI: Vigdis Vandvik and Brian Enquist

*RECITE* -Research and Education Partnership in Climate Change Impacts on Terrestrial Ecosystems. INTPART project 274831 2018 – 2022.
PI: Vigdis Vandvik

**Senter for internasjonalisering av utdanning**
*TraitTrain* - Comparing climate change impacts on High North vs. Alpine ecosystems through research and training in trait-based approaches. SIU project HNP-2015/10037 2016 – 2018
PI: Vigdis Vandvik

*TransPlant* - Research-based traning in experimental climate change plant ecology. UTF-2013/10074 2014 – 2016.
PI: Vigdis Vandvik
